entry.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
entry.summary:
It is not known whether a classical polynomial-time verifier can verify arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computations with an efficient quantum honest prover without computational assumptions. We show that, relative to a classical oracle, such verification is possible for a language beyond the polynomial hierarchy that is decided exactly in quantum polynomial time. The protocol is public-coin, with perfect completeness and soundness error at most 1/4.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #algorithms #cryptography

entry.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
entry.summary:
Agentic Entity Resolution (ER) systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, revise hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may condition later retrieval and produce apparent confirmation. This paper proposes a Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)-informed authorization boundary between evidence available for agent reasoning and evidence eligible to authorize persistent identity-changing mutations.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #ml-theory #cryptography

entry.title: Revisiting Privacy Risks in Quantized Deep Neural Networks
entry.summary:
Model quantization has become a fundamental technique for enabling the efficient deployment of large-scale deep neural networks (DNNs) in data-intensive applications by reducing model size. Despite its widespread adoption, the impact of quantization on training data privacy --- particularly vulnerability to membership inference attacks (MIAs) --- remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive empirical study of privacy risks in quantized DNNs, evaluating eight state-of-the-art MIA attacks across six representative quantization methods.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec #neuroscience

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Capacity-Approaching Pseudorandom Code for Stochastic Edit Channels
entry.summary:
Pseudorandom codes (PRCs) are error-correcting codes whose codewords are computationally indistinguishable from uniformly random strings to any efficient adversary. We study public-key multi-bit PRCs over the stochastic memoryless binary substitution-insertion-deletion channel and its $q$-ary generalization. Here $P_i,P_d$ are the insertion and deletion probabilities, and $P_s$ is the substitution probability conditional on transmission.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Hamming Ideals and Grobner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
entry.summary:
We investigate an algebraic approach to the Syndrome Decoding Problem, based on a reformulation of the Hamming weight constraint and its integration with the Information Set Decoding paradigm. We begin with a systematic analysis of the Hamming variety, deriving its defining equations in terms of elementary symmetric functions. Since these equations may have high degree, we exploit convolution identities for elementary symmetric functions, together with factorizations based on Lucas' identity, to derive an equivalent formulation with auxiliary variables and equations of bounded degree.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: Principles for pRHL Proofs of Cryptographic Protocols: How to Convince EasyCrypt that your Protocol is Secure
entry.summary:
The EasyCrypt proof assistant has been used to successfully formalize security proofs for a wide variety of cryptographic primitives. However, attempts at formalizing objects with interactivity, such as protocols, have fared much worse. In this paper, we investigate (some of) the reasons for this difficulty.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: A gentle introduction to lattice-based cryptography
entry.summary:
We present four quantum-safe schemes: the Kyber (ML-KEM) and FrodoKEM key encapsulation mechanisms, and the Dilithium (ML-DSA) and Falcon (FN-DSA) signature schemes. We also develop the mathematical background on lattices needed to understand why Kyber, FrodoKEM, Dilithium and Falcon are regarded as lattice-based cryptosystems, and we provide insight into the computational hardness of the underlying lattice problems. The exposition is intended to be accessible to senior undergraduate students and beginning graduate students.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: A New Approach to Reducing Modulus Requirements in Homomorphic Computation: Precision Allocation in CKKS
entry.summary:
Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data subject to the prescribed security and precision requirements (allowable deviations from ideal results). Among all FHE schemes, CKKS is a representative scheme for approximate arithmetic, allowing the same operation on multiple values packed into a single RLWE ciphertext. Reducing ciphertext modulus $Q$ for given output precision requirements under RLWE security constraints is a central challenge in homomorphic computation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics
